title: Coalescent as a named backward genealogy
dek: Wikipedia Kingman coalescent: lineages merge backward. A sampling model for gene genealogies, not a dated transmission tree by itself.
story: The coalescent on Wikipedia is a backward-time process: sample n gene copies, wait exponential times for lineages to merge. Kingman's n=2 rate of 1 is the celebrity. It is a population-genetic sampling model.
A TB outbreak transmission tree is a different object (who infected whom). Coalescent times can inform Ne and, with a clock, dates, but they do not print names on edges (stats-transmission-genomics).
Recombination produces an ancestral recombination graph, not a single Kingman tree. Clonal Mtb is closer to one tree; mixed NTM are not.
deep: Effective size Ne rescales time. A bottleneck is not a pretty NJ ladder by itself.
Structured coalescents (migration) are extra parameters, not a Wikipedia lead sentence.
Tajima's D is a sibling summary of the same genealogy (wiki-tajima if present — we may skip if no plate).
Do not call a coalescent date a diagnosis date.

visual.caption: Present samples backward to mergers. Time is coalescent time, not automatically calendar years until a clock is named.
